error_reason: The Orchestrator prematurely accepted that the list of cards banned with Oko was established without opening or verifying the official Wizards of the Coast Nov 18, 2019 announcement. This unverified assumption led the run to proceed with incorrect or unconfirmed inputs for price analysis, culminating in a wrong final answer. Verifying the primary source at that point would have corrected the candidate set and enabled proper data collection, preventing the failure.

hypotheses.rationale: At this step, the Orchestrator asserts that the list of cards banned with Oko has been discovered, but there is no explicit evidence in prior steps that the WebSurfer actually opened and verified the official November 18, 2019 announcement source. This premature acceptance of an unverified list leads directly to proceeding with price collection on an assumed set, and culminates in an unverified final answer. If the Orchestrator had required and verified the primary source (Wizards’ announcement) and then ensured all-time high/low data were actually gathered and compared, the final wrong answer would have been prevented.
hypotheses.check: Verify whether the run has any step that opens and reads the official Wizards of the Coast Nov 18, 2019 Banned & Restricted Announcement and explicitly extracts the full list of Standard bans (Oko, Once Upon a Time, Veil of Summer) before proceeding. Compare claims in step 9 with the actual browsing actions in steps 4 and 8 to confirm the list was not truly verified, and note that no price data were collected before the final answer.

evidence.discrepancy: Step 9 asserts that the ban date and the full list of cards banned with Oko have been discovered, but earlier steps show only search-result snippets and no opening/reading of the official Nov 18, 2019 Wizards B&R announcement. Additionally, despite Step 9 planning to proceed with price data, no pages with actual all-time high/low prices were opened or extracted before the final answer.
